name: Procyon Propellant Works
summary: Methane and oxygen for the surface-to-orbit shuttles. Compressors take CO2 from the atmosphere, electrolysers split water into hydrogen and oxygen, and a Sabatier reactor turns CO2 and hydrogen into methane and water, which goes back to the electrolysers.
since_note: Running before the pioneers landed in April 2070 (book: Mars immigration).
story: The first factory on the Martian surface: it was running before the first pioneers landed in 2070, and by 2075 it covered the propellant needed between the surface and orbit.
process: Atmospheric CO2 acquisition: freezer and compressor trains
PEM water electrolysis, about 53 kWh per kg of hydrogen
Sabatier reactor, CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O, Ru/Al2O3 catalyst at 330 degC
Liquefaction and storage of CH4 and O2

sources.label: Sabatier Carbon Dioxide Reduction Assembly Development for Closed Loop Water Recovery (NASA and Hamilton Sundstrand, 2010)
Mars Design Reference Architecture 5.0, ISRU addendum (NASA SP-2009-566-ADD)
Electrolyser energy use, about 50 to 55 kWh/kg H2 (IEA Global Hydrogen Review)
Mars surface pressure and scale height (NASA Mars Fact Sheet)
